note: WHY A NAMED SET AND NOT A DERIVED ONE. On the SHIPPED compiler all 51 are `loud check reject` and behave exactly like their class-mates — the derived corpus moves 0 of 1,477 classes across the whole family PR and all 1,915 buildable corpus modules are `cmp` byte-identical. What names them is what the CANDIDATE did to them, which nothing reading current behaviour can see: 48 go `loud check reject` -> `check-clean invalid wasm`, and the three witnesses go `loud check reject` -> a check-clean RUNTIME TRAP, which is a column the census records as ZERO across 250,238 cells.

refused.buys: 72 of D11's 184 cells `loud check reject` -> `runs` (the six nested-array reps, both flat records, `new {x:i32}` and the two niche newtypes), and 40 more `loud check reject` -> `loud emit reject`.
refused.candidate: Make an INDEX place narrowable, in four checker rungs: `placeKeyOf` keys `xs[<int literal>]`; `placeCurTy` grows an Index arm (`placeElemTy`, the index twin of `placeFieldTy`); `checkIndexNode` consults the overlay the way `checkMemberNode` already does; and `isPathKey` — which decides overlay-entry vs scope-shadow and tested only for `.` — also accepts `[`. Measured in that order: the first three alone move NOTHING, because a fact keyed `xs[0]` was collected and then installed as a bare-name SHADOW that no reader asks for.
refused.price_trap: THREE check-clean programs that TRAP at run time, each a retirement rule the existing machinery states it does not need BECAUSE index places were unkeyable. `writeRetiresNarrowing`'s own header says it: "An unkeyable target (`xs[i] = …`) names no place and retires nothing — and no narrowing can key one either, so both sides stay consistent." Keying one breaks that invariant three ways: a write through a VARIABLE index (`xs[i] = null`) retires nothing; a write to the ROOT (`xs = [null]`) misses because the prefix leg matches only `tgtKey + "."`, never `tgtKey + "["`; and an ALIASING CALL (`clr(xs)` whose body does `ys[0] = null`) misses because `callInvalidatesReal` tests `key == ak` and `keyHasPrefix(key, ak + ".")`, and the write-effect summaries record no index sub-path.
refused.price_wasm: 48 cells `loud check reject` -> `check-clean INVALID WASM` (`type mismatch: expected i32, found (ref $type)`): the four scalar newtypes and the two three-deep arrays. The checker narrows the index place; the EMITTER has no index-place narrowing channel at all — `memberPathKeyOf` is Member-shaped, `memIsNarrowed` / `memNarrowVariantIndex` only ever look at a Member receiver, and the narrowed READ arms live in `emitMem` — so the boxed element is read at the un-narrowed rep.
refused.verdict: REFUSED at 4bdfcc67. Closing D11 soundly needs the four checker rungs above PLUS an emitter index-place channel PLUS three retirement rungs and their aliasing-call vocabulary — a second landing the size of this whole PR, and one that trades a loud reject for a silent class if any part of it is missing. D11 stays LIVE with its denominator corrected to 184 of 184 (see the row).
